articles.headline: Yemen forces say struck Houthi targets in several areas
articles.summary: AI summary: Yemen's government forces say they hit Houthi positions in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz, while the Houthis claimed a missile and drone strike on a Saudi oil site near Riyadh, where an AFP reporter saw fire and smoke. The renewed civil war, reignited in July, has left heavy casualties around Taiz, and the WFP warns most Yemenis cannot meet basic food needs.

articles.headline: Naqvi accuses KP govt of backing out of counterterrorism commitments
articles.summary: AI summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi says the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government agreed to counterterrorism pledges, including National Action Plan implementation and police reforms, then withdrew from them at the last stage of talks with the Centre. KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi countered by publishing his own draft, saying none of its demands, which covered political dialogue and Imran Khan's detention conditions, were unconstitutional, leaving the talks deadlocked.

political.reason: Collapse of Centre-province talks deepens confrontation between federal and KP governments.

lean.reason: Coverage carries both Naqvi's allegations and Afridi's published rebuttal.

confidence.reason: Reported by three outlets with matching core details, including the KP side's response.

articles.headline: 4 injured Pakistanis rescued from vessel hijacked in Somalia
articles.summary: AI summary: Four Pakistani sailors wounded when Somali forces retook the hijacked tanker MT Honour 25 flew from Addis Ababa to Karachi with the remains of three Pakistani crewmates killed in the operation, after about five months in pirate captivity. PM Shehbaz Sharif announced Rs12.5 million for each bereaved family; the two outlets differ on which Somali force led the rescue and how many pirates were arrested.

political.reason: A consular and humanitarian matter with no effect on governance stability.

confidence.reason: Two outlets agree on the core facts but differ on the rescuing force and number of pirates arrested.

The claims, which Geo's sources also describe as India-backed, come amid a reported surge of militant attacks in KP and have not been independently verified.

PM's adviser Rana Sanaullah warned the march would not be let into Islamabad and that law enforcement would stop any disorder, while PTI leaders gave their own account of the deadlock.
